questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on stating AI's limits honestly, rather than only its strengths?
options: This site's policy is not to oversell what a tool can do or invent content to fill a gap, matching the honesty standard applied throughout the catalog
AI has no real strengths worth mentioning at all
It's required by law to list limitations
The earlier lessons in this chapter were incorrect and need correcting
questions.explain: This mirrors the site's established no-invented-content honesty policy, applied here to AI capability claims.

questions.q: Why can't an LLM recover the 'tribal knowledge' that runs most real production systems?
options: That context lives in people and undocumented history, never in the spec, log, or schema fed into a prompt
Tribal knowledge is always written down in the system's documentation
LLMs can query production systems directly to learn this
This kind of context doesn't actually exist in real systems
questions.explain: Every technique in this chapter worked only from what was explicitly fed to it — no amount of prompting recovers context never given.

questions.q: Why can't an LLM reliably answer a question like whether a returned order should still count toward quarterly revenue?
options: That's a business-logic judgment call that depends on understanding the business, not a fact the LLM can pattern-match from training data or a prompt
The LLM lacks the vocabulary to discuss revenue at all
Revenue questions are mathematically impossible to answer
This is actually a fact the LLM already knows correctly by default
questions.explain: An LLM can draft a plausible-sounding answer, but only the people who own the business logic can know which answer is actually right.

questions.q: What happens when an LLM is asked about a genuinely novel failure with no precedent in its training data?
options: It often produces a confidently wrong answer rather than an honestly uncertain one, because it still generates a plausible-sounding response
It always correctly states that it doesn't know
It refuses to respond at all
It automatically escalates the issue to a human
questions.explain: With no pattern to match against, the model's draft isn't a weak hypothesis — it's often just confidently wrong.

questions.q: What distinguishes a failure an LLM can help diagnose from one it can't, per this lesson?
options: Whether the failure has a documented pattern similar to something in the model's training data
Whether the failure occurred during business hours
Whether the pipeline uses Python or SQL
Whether the failure has ever been logged at all
questions.explain: A repetitive, documented-signature failure is exactly what an LLM pattern-matches well; a truly novel one has nothing to match.
